description:
Hi, I'm Aarav, founder of Horvans, a studio building AI products and web apps. I ship full-stack fast: PHP/Node, React, Three.js,

  and Claude-powered agents with retrieval and citations. We're taking on Flame in Freefall: an AI dashboard that turns decades of

  NASA microgravity fire experiments into ranked, cited safety insights for Moon and Mars crews. Looking for: science folks

  (combustion, physics, aerospace), a Python data wrangler, and a designer/storyteller for the pitch.
summary:
Fire behaves differently in space. Without gravity, flames don't rise; they spread slowly, hide and can keep
  burning in less oxygen than on Earth. On the ISS, acrylic burned at about 15% oxygen, while Earth tests treat
  about 18% as the limit. Yet most spacecraft fire-safety limits still come from tests on Earth. Burn Margin is a
  web app that checks a cabin atmosphere (oxygen, pressure, gravity, airflow) against 37 hand-checked findings from
  NASA microgravity fire experiments and returns BURNS, GOES OUT or NO DATA. Every answer cites the exact row and
  source it came from. It never guesses: if nobody has tested a case (for example, the Moon or Mars), it says NO
  DATA and lists the experiment needed. It also flags oxygen limits that are wrongly reused at a different pressure.
  This matters because Artemis cabins will run at lower pressure and higher oxygen, so materials judged on Earth
  may have less safety margin than engineers think.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Burn Margin answers one question for spacecraft designers and safety reviewers: "In this cabin, will this material

burn, and how sure are we?"

- Burn Verdict: choose a material (acrylic/PMMA, SIBAL fabric, Kevlar/PBI webbing), oxygen %, pressure, gravity

(ISS, Moon, Mars, Earth) and airflow. You get BURNS, GOES OUT or NO DATA, plus the oxygen margin and the rows

used.

- Scorecard: tests each material in real cabins: ISS air, the Artemis exploration atmosphere (34% O2 at 8.2 psia),

a lunar habitat and an Earth lab.

- Pressure Trap: a "% oxygen" limit measured at one pressure does not transfer to another, so the app marks it NOT

TRANSFERABLE.

- Margin Ledger: how many oxygen points each material has before it burns.

- Silent Minutes: in NASA tests the ISS smoke detector missed 50% of Kapton and 67% of Teflon smoke tests.

- Atlas and Next Burn: a map of what has never been tested. Every NO DATA cell becomes a proposed experiment.

- Evidence and Graph: all 37 rows (29 verified, 6 unverified, 2 where sources disagree), linked to NASA sources.

- Ask anything: a local rules engine answers instantly, then Claude answers using only our dataset. Every quote is

checked automatically against its row.

- Worksheet: a one-page evidence sheet for safety reviews (print, Markdown, JSON or link).

HOW IT WORKS

We turned NASA experiment reports (BASS-II, SoFIE, Saffire, FLEX, ACME, NESC TB-26-05, WSTF) into rows: material,

oxygen range, pressure, gravity, flow, value, source and verification status. Only verified, measured limits with

matching conditions decide a verdict (±2 kPa pressure rule). Unverified rows never decide. Untested conditions

return NO DATA instead of a guess.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Engineers see at once where Earth-based limits are not safe to reuse. NASA sees which experiments would close the

biggest gaps before Artemis and Mars. Every number is traceable, so it is usable in real reviews.

CREATIVITY

Most tools give an answer. Ours shows the evidence, and says "no data" when the evidence doesn't exist. That

honesty is the feature.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Node.js, Claude Code / Claude (Anthropic), inline SVG charts, Remotion and ElevenLabs (demo

video), pptxgenjs (slides).
